edges.label: Condign's Former Soviet Union chapter names, dates and assesses SOYUZUFOTSENTR
edges.note: This is the reason the node exists at all. SOYUZUFOTSENTR reaches this board not through Russian ufology literature but through a UK SECRET UK EYES ONLY Defence Intelligence Staff assessment, which places the centre inside a paragraph opening 'It[s] clear that the Former Soviet Union has taken the study of UAPs seriously and th[a]t this may well be related to a programme of understanding and exploiting certain UAP-related natural phenomena, such as plasmas.' The same chapter runs on to Popovich's 1990 All Union Ufology Association at the Air Force Academy, General of Aviation Igor Maltsev's 1990 release of pilot reports, Vsevolod Troitsky of the Russian Academy of Sciences chairing a Commission for the Study of Anomalous Propagation and Phenomena, and Sokolov's account of Soviet aircraft incidents. Condign treats the public centre and the state effort as one national picture. Verified line by line against the released OCR.

b.label: United States Department of Defense (secondary designation: Department of War)

edges.label: opposite reporting posture: mandated versus stigmatised
edges.note: A January 1980 Directive of the Soviet General Staff obliged every serviceman to report any inexplicable phenomenon in writing and routed the results to a single analysis centre, putting the army 'into the on-duty regime of observation' for thirteen years. The contrast with the US chain of command over the same period, where reporting carried career risk and no service-wide collection mandate existed, is the comparison this node exists to make. The Soviet side of the comparison is documented by the programme's own coordinators; no institutional contact between the two is claimed.

edges.label: INFERENCE: the 1990 public centre stands up as the 1978-1990/91 state programme winds down, with Azhazha the common figure
edges.note: READ THE LIMIT BEFORE USING THIS EDGE. No document located in this pass states any transfer of function, records, personnel or authority from SETKA-AN/SETKA-MO to SOYUZUFOTSENTR, and Project Condign - which describes both the Soviet state exploitation programme and SOYUZUFOTSENTR in the same chapter - does not name SETKA at all. What is documented is date adjacency and a shared principal: Condign dates SOYUZUFOTSENTR to 1990; the board dates the SETKA programmes 1978-1990/91; and the board already carries an edge vladimir-azhazha -> setka-program labelled 'ran the parallel public ufology centre after censorship lifted'. This edge makes that existing person-level assertion visible at institution level and nothing more. Reasoning, not evidence. If a later pass finds a document showing a formal succession, re-tier it; if a later pass finds the two were unconnected, delete it without loss.
